reviews.body:
Thanks for this. The zombie and reused-pid cases are real, and both now report not running. Two things need changing before it can merge.

**1. A live service whose command line isn't matched is treated as dead, and its files are deleted.**

`GetState` (`pkg/db/db_local/service.go`) now decides the recorded pid is not the database whenever the command-line match fails. It then removes `steampipe.json`, and on the next call `postmaster.pid`. Postgres notices its lock file is gone and shuts down. Before this PR, state was never removed for a live pid.

The match fails on a live, healthy service in at least two cases:
- On macOS, gopsutil v3.21.11 reads a command line by splitting `ps -o command` output on spaces. With `--install-dir "/Users/me/My Stuff"`, `cmdline[0]` is `/Users/me/My`, so the `postgres` check fails.
- A command-line read that returns an error takes the same path.

So a user with a space in their install path gets `service is not running` from `query`, port-in-use from `start`, and then a stopped service.

When the pid is alive but can't be confirmed, please keep the state and report it as running, as before. Treat it as not running only when you *know* it isn't the database: a zombie, or a readable command line that is clearly some other program. Please also add a test that a live database keeps its state files when its command line can't be matched.

**2. Please reuse `findSteampipePostgresInstances` instead of a second copy of its retry loop.**

`service.go` re-implements the empty-command-line retry from `findSteampipePostgresInstances` (`start_services.go`). Calling that function with a one-process list does the same job and keeps one matcher. Any fix to the macOS split then lands in both places.

**Also needed: a `Changelog:` line** in the PR body. The `shipyard/changelog-line` check fails without one. A suggestion:

> Changelog: `steampipe service status` now reports the service as not running when the database process has exited but is still a zombie, or when its recorded PID now belongs to a different process.

CI is approved to run, so the Linux zombie test gets its first run.

Thanks for working through both points. Both are fixed: a live process whose command line can't be read keeps its state, and the single-process check reuses `findSteampipePostgresInstances`. I also tried a real postgres started from an install path with a space in it, and it is recognised.

Two things still block the merge, both from the stricter `GetState`:

**1. Two existing tests now fail, and a third passes without testing anything.**

```
go test -count=1 -run TestLocalConnection ./pkg/db/db_local/
--- FAIL: TestLocalConnectionStringKeepsSpecialCharacters
    create_connection_test.go:33: failed to build connection string: steampipe service is not running
--- FAIL: TestLocalConnectionStringKeepsSSLPassphraseOutOfLog
    create_connection_test.go:59: failed to build connection string: steampipe service is not running
```

These came with #5183. Their helper `setUpLocalSSLService` (`create_connection_test.go:110`) saves the running info with `os.Getpid()`, which is the test binary and not a postgres. So `GetState` now drops the state. `TestLocalConnectionErrorsHideSSLPassphrase` still passes, but only because every error it checks is "service is not running", raised before the passphrase is read. It needs to fail if the passphrase leaks, so please make sure it reaches the code it was written for.

Fix: have `setUpLocalSSLService` start the stand-in with `startFakeDatabase` and save that pid, and set `app_specific.AppName = "steampipe"`, as `service_test.go` does.

**2. Lint fails.** CI's golangci-lint reports a new finding (Test Linting run on this head):

```
pkg/db/db_local/running_info.go:122:21: G703: Path traversal via taint analysis (gosec)
```

The taint starts at `stop_services_test.go:108`: the command built from `os.Args[0]` is passed to `newRunningDBInstanceInfo` and then saved. Passing `&exec.Cmd{Process: &os.Process{Pid: service.Process.Pid}}` instead, as `writeStateForPid` does, clears it.

**Also:** the CLA check is still pending. We can only merge once it's signed (the CLA assistant link is in the comment above).

Once you push, I'll start CI on it straight away.

Thanks, both fixes are right. The connection-string tests now run against a stand-in database, so `TestLocalConnectionErrorsHideSSLPassphrase` checks the passphrase path again, and lint is clean. `go test ./pkg/db/...` passes on e73d54b4, and CI is green.

The only thing left is the CLA: please sign it through the CLA assistant link above. Once it's green I'll merge.

comments.body:
[![CLA assistant check](https://cla-assistant.io/pull/badge/signed)](https://cla-assistant.io/turbot/steampipe?pullRequest=5160)
All committers have signed the CLA.

Thanks, both points are addressed. (1) The state is kept when the pid is alive but the command line cannot be read, and it is dropped only for a zombie or when the readable command line is not the steampipe database. A space in the install path is handled in `isSteampipePostgresProcess`: a `postgres` or `postgres.exe` basename in a later argument, together with `application_name=steampipe`, is still this service, so start and stop use the same match as status. A different postgres without that argument is not. (2) `GetState` calls `findSteampipePostgresInstances` for the recorded pid instead of keeping its own retry loop. The PR body now has the Changelog line for the shipyard check.

The nilerr lint (Test Linting, service.go) is fixed without changing that behavior. A failed or empty command-line read is stored in a bool and still reports the pid as running; the nil error is returned outside the `err != nil` branch, so nilerr is quiet. `golangci-lint run ./pkg/db/db_local/` now reports only the preexisting G703 in `running_info.go`.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
Merged the latest `develop` into this branch to resolve the conflict; no other changes.

Thanks, both are addressed in e73d54b. (1) `setUpLocalSSLService` now starts the stand-in with `startFakeDatabase`, saves that pid and sets `app_specific.AppName = "steampipe"`, as `service_test.go` does. `TestLocalConnectionStringKeepsSpecialCharacters` and `TestLocalConnectionStringKeepsSSLPassphraseOutOfLog` pass again, and `TestLocalConnectionErrorsHideSSLPassphrase` now gets past the service check: each of the three errors it inspects is the TLS key decryption failure (`x509: decryption password incorrect`) from the wrong passphrase, not "service is not running". (2) `startOlderVersionService` passes `&exec.Cmd{Process: &os.Process{Pid: service.Process.Pid}}` to `newRunningDBInstanceInfo`, as `writeStateForPid` does, for the G703 finding.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks for working through the review. One thing left before we can merge: please sign the Contributor License Agreement at https://cla-assistant.io/turbot/steampipe?pullRequest=5160. The check turns green once it's signed.
